intended_object: A thin quiver: a quiver with at most one arrow between any two vertices, i.e. one with no parallel arrows. This is taken from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The body says that for all vertices a and b, the type of arrows a ⟶ b is a subsingleton. That means it has at most one element, so there are no two distinct parallel arrows. This is exactly the standard notion of a thin quiver, and its categorical version is a thin category. The definition is stated for an arbitrary quiver, which is its natural generality, and it covers the degenerate cases correctly: an empty hom-type is allowed, and so is a type with no vertices. Mathlib has no separate definition of this notion. Mathlib's thin categories are built on this very definition, so no other counterpart applies.
